stirling-small-demand-worklist.text:
# Stirling: small demand frontiers and large local work

Runtime: `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`. Final status: TIMEOUT. Latest reached run-6; latest complete run-5; latest accepted forward report run-5.

## What the numbers mean

Run-5 starts from the 13,901 selected demand memberships produced by run-4. It runs for 612.328s and produces 1,304 selected demand memberships. Run-6 starts from those 1,304 rows and times out after 393.611s.

Demand storage restricts initial admission and selected summary output. It does not restrict every local instruction visit. The input and output frontiers therefore do not bound local work.

| Current counter | run-5 | run-6 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Incoming selected demand memberships |13,901|1,304|
| Method input arrival callbacks |272,759|1,280,154|
| Successful restricted C2 intersection outputs |23,930|9,298|
| Fresh initial admissions, including ZERO |8,647|7,914|
| Fresh subscription-input admissions, including ZERO-only |189,337|581,374|
| Native record crossings with a produced result |304,527|Incomplete frontier unavailable|
| Nonzero-initial method actors |214|Incomplete frontier unavailable|
| ZERO-only method actors |7,043|Incomplete frontier unavailable|
| Last logged completed reservation count |95,294|364,294|

The last event counts are lower bounds on completed reservations by that log instant, not final instruction counts. Source counter deltas use END minus START from the closed phase evidence. A fresh initial admission is not necessarily a concrete initial: ZERO is included.

The final frontier is available only for complete run-5. Do not invent a run-6 frontier from the latest progress sample.

## Current repeat gate has a short lifetime

The later-run worklist has no pending tree union. Changed deltas enter the `other` list. Unchanged deltas enter an unchanged LIFO lane with a repeat set:

```kotlin
// DeltaWorklist.kt
fun addUnchanged(delta: EdgeDelta): Boolean {
    val key = ordinaryDeltaOrDeltaWithProtectionMask(delta)
    if (!seen.add(key)) return false
    unchanged += delta
    return true
}

fun afterProcess() {
    if (unchangedEmpty) seen.clear()
}
```

The clear condition does not test whether changed work remains. The set protects one uninterrupted unchanged traversal, not the whole run or the whole method relation.

Also, unchanged propagation bypasses `MethodEdgeStore.add`:

```kotlin
// Changed result:
edges.add(successor, premise, facts)?.let { push(EdgeDelta(premise, successor, it)) }

// Unchanged result:
worklist.addUnchanged(EdgeDelta(item.premise, successor, item.facts))
```

Thus the method store cannot suppress a repeated unchanged visit at a common downstream node when the two arrivals came from different already-admitted producer nodes.

## Finite duplicate-work witness

This code is a mechanism example, not the identified hot Stirling method. Assume both source occurrences are selected. The source rule marks its returned object exactly with the same full mark T.

```java
void example(int choice) {
    Box x;
    if (choice == 0) {
        x = sourceT();
        // Changed admission at L: ZERO -> x.$/T, NORMAL.
        int leftOnly = 1;
    } else {
        x = sourceT();
        // Changed admission at R: ZERO -> x.$/T, NORMAL.
        int rightOnly = 2;
    }
    // Common node C. No local store admission is required for unchanged hops.
    int a0 = 0;
    int a1 = a0;
    // ... a long chain of assignments unrelated to x ...
    sinkT(x);
}
```

After the ZERO/control traversal has registered both source outputs, a permitted worklist state is:

```text
changed: [L/F, R/F]
unchanged: []
F = (complete premise ZERO, x.$/T NORMAL, same protection)

pop R/F
  -> unchanged C/F -> ... -> sink/F
  -> unchanged lane empty: clear seen
     changed L/F is still pending

pop L/F
  -> C/F is accepted again
  -> repeat the same common chain and sink evaluation
```

The source locations remain separately recorded at their source hooks. The duplicate work here is the downstream traversal of an equal relation, not a request to remove a source occurrence.

A finite executable model of the current lane ordering is saved at `/tmp/stirling-unchanged-worklist-witness.py`:

```text
2 changed producers, 3 common neutral nodes:
  changed process entries = 2
  unchanged process entries = 6
  each common node visited twice
  unique sink observation = 1

100 changed producers, 100 common neutral nodes:
  changed process entries = 100
  unchanged process entries = 10,000
  unique sink observation = 1
```

This establishes an avoidable-work pattern in the current queue contract. It does not establish that this pattern accounts for the actual 612s. The current measurements do not record repeated exact keys across repeat-set epochs.

There is a second limitation: the repeat key is a complete Facts value. Packets `{x.f/T}` and `{x.f/T,x.g/T}` are different keys. The first membership can be revisited even without a clear when a later packet overlaps an earlier packet. A count of fact packets is not a count of newly processed relation memberships.

## This is not a proof of an infinite unchanged loop

A pure unchanged cycle retains its repeat set while the next unchanged successor is queued:

```text
C/F -> D/F -> E/F -> C/F
last offer C/F is rejected
queue becomes empty; then seen is cleared
no item remains to restart the cycle
```

The executable model confirms one source and a three-node unchanged cycle terminate after three unchanged process entries. Two distinct producer waves execute the cycle twice, then terminate.

No source-level infinite loop has been found in `DeltaWorklist` alone. The complete current analyzer termination proof is outside this small witness. A true repeated-state bug elsewhere remains possible until the hot owner and its state growth are observed.

## The scheduler counters cannot supply instruction counts

The runner quantum is 1,000. But a quantum yield keeps the same Work reservation:

```kotlin
if (complete) run.afterHandler()
else queue.add(event) // No handled-count increment.
```

`RunMethodAnalyzer.work` can also yield on a ZERO-phase change. Therefore:

- Do not multiply the logged 95,294 events by 1,000.
- A stable one-in-flight count can be one Work reservation with many quantum yields.
- A completed Work event can process a short tail or many quanta. Other completed reservations include links, deliveries and the start-batch reservation.
- One in-flight reservation at each 10s sample does not prove one method owner remains active for the whole interval.

59 of the 61 run-5 progress samples report one in-flight reservation; the other sampled counts are {1: 59, 2: 2}. From the first to last sampled count, completed reservations increase by 59,660 over about 600.024s, about 99.43/s. That does not give a nontrivial instruction-process lower bound because event kinds and quantum-return reasons are not logged.

If a diagnostic records **QUANTUM** yields separately from phase yields, each such later-run yield can establish 1,000 processed work units, subject to counting resume items separately. Exact `steps` values already count scalar `process` entries in later runs. Those per-actor step values are not exported in the current report.

## Existing full-window profiles support local work, not a cheap-operation diagnosis

The existing closed run-5 JFR window contains 47,990 Java execution samples. Inclusive shares:

```text
RunMethodAnalyzer.process             97.93%
emitUnchanged                        36.70%
DeltaWorklist.addUnchanged            13.13%
MethodEdgeStore.add                    2.43%
```

The run-5 sampled allocation estimate is 947.80 GiB over the window, while total GC pause interval union is 0.899s. The profile indicates many short-lived processing objects. The estimate is not retained memory and is not an exact allocation counter.

Run-6 is a different workload. Its existing full-window JFR has 61,065 Java execution samples:

```text
RunMethodCallServices.process         83.24%
MethodEdgeStore.add                   65.96%
intersectTaintMask                    55.70%
emitUnchanged                         3.36%
```

The run-6 sampled allocation estimate is 2,339.12 GiB. Native/GC CPU is not included in this Java-only denominator. The separate 30s native profile shows 40.69% collector-worker samples. These windows must not be combined as one additive percentage table.

Both runs can do much more work than their selected demand count suggests. These data support tracing repeated local relations and their protection masks, not a proposal merely to make call detection or hashing faster.

## Actual hot method and shape remain unknown

The Java profiles identify analyzer functions. They do not record the `RunMethodAnalyzer.key` value, the current program instruction, the original premise or the current fact tree. The compact frontier reports method sets/counts after the run, not per-method process traffic. Neither a generic profile stack nor the one-in-flight count identifies the hot application method.

The old Stirling heap showing a generated dispatcher and many statics is historical evidence only. It is not evidence that the current run-5 owner or fact is static. No current heap was captured because no OOM occurred.

## Minimal diagnostic needed next

Use a separate same-config diagnostic run on the same runtime source. Do not change transfer, demand, field, mark or summary semantics.

At method-owner boundaries, record:

```text
method key; run; direction; field limit
processed changed / processed unchanged
work calls; complete returns; QUANTUM yields; ZERO-phase yields
changed/unchanged queue sizes and peaks
unchanged offers; accepted; rejected
repeat-set clears; clears while changed work remains; size before clear
recordCrossings; fresh initial count with ZERO split
```

For the actual hot owner, sample full qualified fact descriptions:

```text
instruction index; complete original premise
FLOW/TAINT/REACH; layer; static/nonstatic base
tail; field exclusion; mark exclusion
sampled field paths and full marks; protection present/coordinates
```

Add a bounded exact-key diagnostic sample to distinguish:

```text
same node + premise + header + ordinary tree + protection,
seen before a clear and processed again after it
```

Use complete key equality, not a hash-only duplicate claim. Label bounded-sample counts as lower bounds. A stronger membership-overlap check can be enabled only for the identified hot node, so the diagnostic itself does not enumerate every tree in the project.

The decision follows those measurements:

- Repeated equal relations across unchanged epochs: avoid repeated neutral traversal and retain a proved boundary membership gate.
- Mostly new memberships: identify why one small admitted demand expands to that large local relation.
- Run-6 mostly equal ordinary roots with mask work: trace the protected coordinates and repeated annotation processing separately.

The next report must show actual hot method, fact shape, process counts and relation growth. Until then, exact current attribution remains unproved.

Source-bound receipt: `/tmp/stirling-small-demand-worklist.json`. It includes source hashes, exact counter deltas, current JFR frame rows and the finite witness output.

stirling-small-demand-eligibility.text:
# Stirling: a small demand frontier does not bound current execution

Date: 29 October 2026.
Runtime: `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`.
Latest reached: **run-6**. Latest complete and accepted forward: **run-5**.
Status: source and closed-artifact investigation. No analyzer or reader was run.

## 1. Measured distinction

| Receiving run | Input entry rows | Input paired rows | Engine seconds | C2 input arrivals | C2 emitted offers | Fresh initials |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| run-5, forward, limit4 | 11,525 | 13,901 | 612.328 | 272,759 | 23,930 | 8,647 |
| run-6, backward, limit5 | 630 | 1,304 | 393.611 TIMEOUT | 1,280,154 | 9,298 | 7,914 |

The outgoing run-5 frontier has1,304 demand memberships in156 MethodKeys.
Run-5 has214 actors with a nonzero initial and7,043 classified `zeroOnly`.
It has304,527 productive native record crossings. Incoming run-5 source seeds
are produced at the run-4 barrier; its frontier reports900 seed entries. The77
seeds reported after run-5 belong to the next backward run. Do not interchange
these frontiers.

The C2 counters are per-run END minus START. `restrictedIntersections` counts
initial offers returned by the demand lookup, not successful input-arrival
queries. One input can offer several initials. `newInitials` also counts direct
root/backward-ZERO starts, so it is not a count of new concrete demand queries.

Run-5 `initialCandidates27649 - restrictedIntersections23930 =3719`. The other
root audit identifies3,719 configured roots restarted in every iteration. In
forward runs, these direct root ZERO attempts account for that difference.
They are not selected by the13,901 demand pairs.

The important CPU evidence is that demand lookup itself is already small:

| Whole-run Java family membership | run-5 | run-6 |
|---|---:|---:|
| C2 | 0.0292% | 0.0393% |
| C5 | 0.0104% | 0.0033% |
| Demand total | 0.0396% | 0.0426% |
| Call pipeline | 19.6666% | 83.2474% |
| Protection | 0.0042% | 55.7406% |

These Java families overlap. The saved run-5 native middle window instead shows
unchanged routing and call detection. Neither observation supports spending this
iteration on a faster small demand index. The work occurs after or outside its
admission decision.

## 2. What C2 actually limits

The source pipeline is:

```text
caller fact at a call
  -> bind input
  -> subscribe(callee, callerRef, actual)
       -> admit current input
       -> replay existing current publications
       -> replay old native records and reversed views, if restricted
  -> LinkIn(callee, callerRef, actual)
       -> cut actual to this run's limit
       -> C2: intersect actual with local demand
       -> start fresh method initial(s), if any
```

`RunMethodCallServices.enterCallees` sends `subscribe` before `link`.
Production `ProtocolSteps.Inline` executes the replay during subscription.
`SubscriptionManager.replayRecords` does not ask C2 for permission. It uses
native `applicable || inside`, then applies the old complete relation and resumes
the caller. A native result can therefore cause caller work even when the callee
later rejects every nonzero C2 initial.

C2 is a gate for **new method body initials**. It is not a per-instruction demand
filter, a bound on current caller work, or a predicate for native record reuse.
C5 is a publication restriction at the summary boundary. It does not prevent the
preceding local body computation. A raw NORMAL summary can still enter native
storage independently of what its C5 publication kept.

Source references:

```text
engine/RunMethodCallServices.kt: enterCallees, applyRecord, applyRecordView,
                                resumeCallees, applyParts
engine/SubscriptionManager.kt: subscribe, replay, replayRecords
engine/RunMethodAnalyzer.kt: addLink, addInitial, retainSummary, published
store/DemandStore.kt: initials, intersect
store/RecordStore.kt: persist, byEntry, byExit
```

## 3. ZERO and native effects are outside explicit demand row counts

There are four different ZERO paths:

```text
root Start -> addRootZero -> addInitial(ZERO)
  No C2 selection.

forward callee receives Reach ZERO -> C2 implicit zeroDemand
  This implicit entry exists even when that method has no explicit demand rows.

backward reached callee -> ZeroIn -> addZeroEntry -> addInitial(ZERO)
  No C2 selection.

backward ZERO-premise requirement summary -> balanced caller ZERO subscription
  No C5 restriction or ordinary satisfaction test.
```

A forward call's control can also pass the call through `zeroCanReturn`. Current
`JIRCallPlanBuilder` sets it from a resolved/unresolved/predefined target policy;
it is not the number of current demand rows. Do not interpret the small demand
frontier as a control-reachability frontier.

A `zeroOnly` actor means only `!actor.nonZeroInitial`. It can have:

- a ZERO initial and many marked `ZERO -> x/T` intermediate facts;
- a ZERO initial and only control facts;
- no initial at all, after LinkIn created its core and C2 rejected the input.

Thus7,043 `zeroOnly` actors do not prove7,043 marked body analyses, or7,043 cheap
control-only walks. An exact count needs a per-actor census. Do not subtract all
7,257 actors from8,647 fresh initials and call the remainder the exact nonzero
initial count.

The diagnostic `zeroOnlyEdges` also understates instruction traffic. Frontier
sums `actor.edgeDeltas`, not `actor.steps`. `emitUnchanged` routes the same fact to
successors through `worklist.addUnchanged`, without `MethodEdgeStore.add`, and
does not increment `edgeDeltas`. Each processed unchanged item still increments
`steps` and performs call detection/form access/routing. A small edge diagnostic
can coexist with many unchanged instruction hops.

`DeltaWorklist.seen` covers one active unchanged-wave interval. `afterProcess`
clears it when all unchanged lanes empty, even if changed producers remain.
Another producer can later route an equal fact over the same neutral region.
This prevents neither K producer waves times N untouched instructions nor all
repeated native replay continuations. The separate worklist investigation has a
finite example of this amplification. It is not an assertion of an infinite loop.
Run-5 actually completes.

## 4. Native reuse is intentionally not demand-restricted in the original AP contract

The current code follows these clauses:

```text
ap.md section8.7 R4:
  native records apply by applicable || inside; they are not restricted.

ap.md section8.7 R5:
  records remain available even when internal sources are not next-run seeds.
  a record/read view never grants a new method initial.

ap.md section9.2:
  backward ZERO enters reached callees directly;
  ZERO-premise backward summaries return through balanced caller ZERO,
  without restriction or satisfaction.
```

There is no evidence here of a new C2/native eligibility violation. Rather, the
current contract allows a large **known NORMAL execution fringe** around a small
unresolved demand frontier. The fringe can carry concrete marked facts under a
ZERO origin and can walk bodies or caller continuations without creating new
callee demand. Source seeding limits new source actions; it does not invalidate
an older complete normal source record.

A backward normal native `ret/T -> ZERO` can also be read forward as
`ZERO -> ret/T`. This is an additional allowed native source producer, not a
new body initial. A normal forward `ZERO -> ret/T` record is already sufficient
for the example below.

## 5. Code example: no new demand, but N unchanged marked hops

The following is a mechanism example. It is not yet the identified hot Stirling
method. All source/sink rules are explicit. `oldSourceT()` assigns T exactly at
its result. No rule observes the counter fields. Another branch has the current
U demand, so the analyzer performs another forward run.

```java
// Previous precise forward run-3 used its selected source seed here.
Box oldProducer() {
    return oldSourceT();
}
// Retained NORMAL native relation after run-3:
// ZERO -> ret.$/T.
// This must NOT be described as a run-1 normal TAINT record:
// current run-1 forces all TAINT results to DEMAND.

// Run-5 local explicit demand: none.
// Run-5 selected Source seeds in this subtree: none.
Box noise() {
    Box x = oldProducer();
    // Caller ZERO subscription reads the old native record.
    // ZERO -> x.$/T, NORMAL, is emitted in noise without a nonzero C2 initial.

    Metrics.c0 = 0; // Does not touch x: unchanged ZERO -> x.$/T.
    Metrics.c1 = 1; // Same fact takes another unchanged hop.
    // ... N distinct observable field stores that do not touch x ...
    Metrics.cN = N;

    return x;
}
// A raw NORMAL ZERO -> ret.$/T can be inferred again.
// Its current C5 publication can be empty. No new demand is required.
// Native persistence can deduplicate the already-known complete summary.

void main() {
    noise(); // Result is ignored. ZERO still enters the method.
    refineCurrentUCandidate();
}
```

Returning x keeps its local use real. Observable counter writes prevent a
compiler from erasing the whole neutral region. Those stores do not read/write
x, so FormApplier reports x untouched. The example needs no static taint mark.
A small unchanged/demand count does not remove those N instruction visits.

Even a normal native summary for `noise` does not currently suppress its ZERO
body start. Calling it can both reuse its known normal summary and walk its ZERO
body again. The new source gate prevents a new oldSourceT action in that body,
but the nested native `oldProducer` record can still recreate T.

Now repeat this shape in M roots/call contexts or supply K fresh producer waves.
The unresolved demand set can remain unchanged while body/continuation work grows
with M, K and N. Fresh packet headers, concrete path width and field-limit depth
add further dimensions. The frontier is not a complexity bound for those products.

## 6. Why a direct native-demand gate would be wrong

```java
// Retained NORMAL FLOW native summary from run-1:
// p.*/FLOW -> ret.*/FLOW.
Box id(Box p) { return p; }

void main() {
    Box x = selectedSourceT();
    Box y = id(x);
    sinkT(y);
}
```

The complete native id relation creates no callee demand under R1/F77. Its
C2 nonzero admission may be empty. Native application must nevertheless give
y/T to the caller and sink. `if no local demand then skip native records` loses
this required route. Filtering every native result by its callee demand has the
same problem. It would be a semantic change, not an optimization of C2.

The analogous backward blanket ZERO gate loses a sink in a helper with no normal
return. This is why the balanced ZERO rule remains necessary. A `zeroOnly` flag
is not a certificate that the method has no relevant internal observation.

## 7. Avoidable work and the needed contract

The source confirms two work-removal directions:

1. **Same-relation repetition:** native replay batches, caller continuations and
   unchanged producer waves can traverse the same geometry repeatedly. Coalescing
   exact compatible packets or routing a certified neutral region can remove
   repeated visits without discarding the fringe's relations. Root/premise/header
   and protection must remain exact. Packet merging alone cannot remove every
   untouched hop; there can be only one pending packet at a time.
2. **Certified ZERO execution shortcut:** avoid a method's ZERO body when its
   complete control/effect/observation contract is already known. A normal ZERO
   return record by itself is insufficient. The certificate must account for
   selected source/sink seeds, entry/exit/unconditional observations, native ZERO
   generators, transitive calls, exceptional/normal reachability and any unknown
   ZERO-origin effect that still needs refinement. Reproduce required effects and
   observations at the boundary. Do not simply treat all `zeroOnly` actors as neutral.

To restrict the known normal fringe more aggressively, the design needs an
explicit relevance contract: which complete old results/reports remain available
without executing them again, and how to prove a dropped result cannot reach a
current demand or observation. That contract is not present in C2/C5 today.
A method-entry demand check alone cannot establish it. Do not add such a gate
silently while optimizing summary storage or initial emission.

## 8. Minimal diagnostic replay needed to identify the actual hot owner

Current profiles identify the hot operations but not which method, premise or
fact header owns the hundreds of seconds. No saved per-edge first-loss/work ledger
proves that `noise` is the actual Stirling pattern. An isolated same-source replay
is justified. Keep16g, FULL,1,1,2,...,1080s and the same project/rules. Label its
numbers diagnostic; do not replace the primary measurements with them.

Use runner-owned scalar counters, not global atomic counters on every hop:

```text
per actor:
  existing steps, edgeDeltas, recordCrossings, demandLayerEdges;
  fresh ZERO and nonzero initials, separately;
  direct root ZERO attempts, backward ZeroIn attempts, C2 ZERO offers;
  processed Reach-control vs ZERO-origin TAINT/FLOW vs nonzero-origin data;
  emitUnchanged offers, admitted hops, repeat rejects and wave resets;
  native applications/results by stored direction and ZERO/nonzero premise;
  caller resume/result-packet counts, because callbacks are not actor.steps;
  point-store fresh versus duplicate admissions.
```

Dump the top owners by processed/unchanged/native work, including timeout actors
before release. A very small bounded sample can keep method signature, instruction
index, original kind, conclusion base kind, tail, bounded path prefix, header and
protection presence. Do not call eager `ops.leaves` on a large tree. Walk at most
a fixed number of nodes/leaves and record that truncation. Do not retain IR objects
or old complete Facts trees in an unbounded diagnostic table.

This replay will separate three possibilities: broad root/ZERO control walks,
ZERO-origin marked native fringe, and a few demanded nonzero bodies with many
packet/path waves. Only then select the largest algorithmic work removal.

stirling-small-demand-zero-shortcut.text:
# ZERO-body reuse and unchanged-fringe removal

Date: 2026-10-29. Runtime reference: `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`.
Scope: source audit and proposed contracts only. No production change or analyzer launch.
Latest accepted Stirling run is run-5; run-6 timed out. The diagnostic replay has reached run-5 and is still running while this note is written.

## Decision

Do not infer that an ordinary method has a complete semantic model from its NORMAL native records. Do not skip its ZERO body solely because it has no selected source/sink seeds or few demand rows. A complete model for the current semantic inputs can replace the body, but it must include internal observations and ZERO contributions to mixed joins, as well as boundary summaries. The existing record store does not provide that certificate.

The fresh diagnostic evidence makes this a secondary direction. At approximately 100 s of diagnostic run-5, `PipelineProcessor` has 147 initials (1 ZERO, 21 FLOW, 125 TAINT), about 239.8 million steps and 238.8 million unchanged operations; only about 84 thousand STATIC operations, maximum observed root width 7, and no protected facts. A tiny biased LRU sample already witnessed about 1.17 million repeated complete visited keys. These are interim diagnostic counters supplied by the parent, not whole-run counts or an unbiased duplicate percentage. The primary next contract should remove repeated unchanged cones for nonzero relations too.

## What current ZERO analysis does

* `RunMethodAnalyzer.addRootZero` and backward `addZeroEntry` admit ZERO directly. A forward callee ZERO link also passes the implicit `DemandStore.zeroDemand`.
* `RunMethodCallServices.enterCallees` subscribes before it links the callee (lines 317–325). Restricted native replay occurs inside that subscription, independently of the later C2 emission decision.
* A NORMAL native record remains available even when its old source is not selected in this forward run: `spec/ap.md` R4/R5, lines 2768–2796. This is deliberate. An empty local demand index does not make that effect irrelevant to the caller.
* Source execution is seed-gated (`EngineAlgebra.allowsSource`; `RunMethodLocalServices.sourcePredicateActionsAt`). Forward sink checks are not seed-gated (`RunMethodLocalServices.checkSinksAt`, lines 217–275). Backward sink seeds are a separate operation.
* Untouched facts use `emitUnchanged` (analyzer lines 576–583). This bypasses `MethodEdgeStore.add`, but still executes each successor instruction. Its repeat set is cleared whenever unchanged lanes are empty, including when changed producers remain (`DeltaWorklist.afterProcess`, lines 123–126).
* `zeroOnly` is not a no-work certificate. It means no nonzero initial was admitted. It can include many marked ZERO-origin local facts, or even an empty actor after a rejected link.

These facts explain why small C2/C5 frontiers do not bound method-body work. They do not establish which mechanism dominates a project without owner telemetry.

## The focused executable fixture

The diagnostic-only `SmallDemandNativeNeutralWorkTest.kt` represents:

```java
Object oldProducer() { return sourceT(); }
void noise() {
    Object x = oldProducer();
    scratch = null; // N unrelated ordinary instructions
    // x is dead; no sink or returned marked value.
}
```

It first derives a real NORMAL `ZERO -> ret.$/T` summary in run-3 with its source seed. It retains only that inferred native record. Run-5 uses FULL mode, field limit 4, REPEAT_RUN1, an empty explicit demand store and no source seeds.

Current behavior is: native replay creates `ZERO -> x.$/T`, every initial remains ZERO, the current producer source is suppressed, and the marked local visits all N unrelated instructions without producing a marked method summary. Controls use N=1 and N=9 with and without the native record. The mandatory marked-neutral visits grow by eight while demand stays empty. This is a finite workload example, not evidence that all native outputs can be dropped.

## Counterexamples to a seed-only shortcut

### An internal sink has no return-summary representation

```java
void consumeOld() {
    Object x = oldProducer(); // native NORMAL ZERO -> x.$/T
    sinkT(x);                // observed although consumeOld has no source seed
}
```

The return-summary set may contain only ZERO control. It does not describe the sink. A previously saved observation list is sufficient only if it is complete for the *current* records and rules. A new native `ZERO -> ret/T` record can appear after the earlier cache evaluation, so an older empty observation list cannot certify this call.

### ZERO evidence can join a newly admitted nonzero fact

```java
// Current submitted p/U is admitted by one selected demand.
void combine(Object p) {
    Object z = oldProducer(); // ZERO -> z.$/T, source itself not selected now
    joinedSink(z, p);         // CM(z,T) AND CM(p,U)
}
```

If ZERO execution is removed and only ordinary boundary NORMAL records are reused, the current `p/U` walk cannot supply the missing `z/T` literal. The sink has no required return value. A prior list of all-ZERO observations cannot repair this mixed binding. The same issue occurs for a conditional rule which assigns to an observable position.

The minimal repair is either to retain/replay ZERO support at the join site, or to provide a complete *conditional* observation/transfer model which accepts the new nonzero input. A flat list of old sink reports is not such a model. `ConjunctionStore` and `RulePredicateStore` currently retain inputs so that the later fresh member triggers a join; that persistence is also why replaying an already processed identical first member is unnecessary.

### Local absence of seeds is weaker than subtree absence

```java
void wrapper() { helper(); }
void helper() { selectedSource(); }
```

`wrapper` has no source seed, but its ZERO call walk reaches the selected one. Backward ZERO discovery has the analogous example with a selected sink seed in a callee. Prescan reachability must include the full context-resolved call graph, roots, boundary rules and predefined-call behavior; a local seed test is insufficient.

## Sufficient transparent ZERO-reuse certificate

For one full MethodKey and direction, a body replacement needs all of these properties:

```text
ZeroModel {
    semanticInputVersion;
    completeZeroBoundaryRelations;   // normal + required demand, geometry/E/layer/protection
    completeZeroObservations;        // rule occurrence/proof/witness support, not callback counts
    mixedJoinSupportOrConditionalModels;
    completeDiscoveryEffects;       // selected descendants and required control reachability
}
```

1. The model is complete for the current forms, filters, call contexts, direction, field limit, demand admission/restriction policy, selected seeds and immutable record snapshot. Reusing an older result requires a proved validity test, not merely monotone record retention.
2. Every omitted ZERO-origin summary publication is either reproduced with ordinary C5 behavior or already usable at the caller through unchanged native R4/R5 behavior. Do not turn replay into an initial emission.
3. Every omitted internal observation and every required ZERO contribution to a later mixed join is reproduced. All relevant fact geometry, field and mark exclusions, layers, and non-subsumable annotations are retained.
4. Discovery of selected descendant seeds and future admitted inputs still occurs. A suppressed ZERO start must not prevent required call subscriptions/links or backward ZERO discovery without an equivalent replacement.
5. New publication/input effects invalidate the relevant cache or enter it as deltas until a fixed point. Absence of observations must itself be certified complete. A native record store is neither a complete summary set nor a dependency-version cache.

Under this certificate, replace each maximal omitted ZERO derivation by its modeled boundary/observation/join effect. The model reproduces the same input/output pairs and retained observations; remaining derivations then proceed by the unchanged ordinary rules. Induction on finite derivation height gives no missing effect, and the reverse inclusion follows because each modeled effect has an omitted ordinary derivation. Recursive calls need the corresponding least-fixed-point certificate. This is a proposal proof obligation, not an existing theorem or implementation claim.

A stricter cheap subcase is a certified ZERO-inert region: it has no active zero source, no applicable zero-origin data producer, no ZERO-observing rule, and no selected discovery target. ZERO then carries only control. Reachability can replace instruction-by-instruction control traversal. This subcase excludes the native-marked fringe in the fixture and does not address the measured nonzero `PipelineProcessor` explosion.

## Higher-priority removal: repeated unchanged cones

The measured work calls for this run-local contract first:

```text
visitKey = (full MethodKey, full original premise, instruction,
            exact Facts value, exact nonSubsumable mask)

After a visitKey has been processed:
    identical unchanged re-arrival adds no semantic information.
    A fresh fact, protection upgrade, publication or join member is separate delta work.
```

The mask is mandatory: ordinary `EdgeDelta` equality excludes annotation metadata, so the existing worklist uses a separate `RepeatKey(delta, mask)`.

Why later events do not require rerunning an identical unchanged input:

* ordinary forms and source permissions are fixed for the run;
* predicate/conjunction inputs remain stored, so a new other member triggers the missing combination;
* an existing call subscription receives later fresh summaries; its old input need not traverse to the call again;
* native records are immutable during the run;
* unchanged propagation preserves the same premise, facts, layer, E and mask.

The present temporary repeat set proves only within-wave suppression. It does not establish whole-run idempotence because it forgets old keys as soon as unchanged lanes empty. A new changed producer can therefore re-enter the same neutral cone. A finite K-producer/N-node cone can perform K×N instruction visits even though only one normalized relation is semantically new at its join.

Do not immediately store every unchanged intermediate in MethodEdgeStore: this could replace the CPU explosion with large retained state. Candidate implementations must compare persistent per-boundary admission, a relation-to-neutral-region summary, and conservative jumps to the next relevant operations. The boundary must retain rule checks, calls touched by the fact, normal/exceptional exits, and any side effect required by current forms; an ordinary untouched node can be skipped. Dead-local output filtering is another strict subcase only after proving no reachable transfer/rule/alias/boundary can observe that local.

Before implementation, use the live diagnostic to quantify complete-key repeats and hot owner/base families, then test mixed joins and late publications explicitly. This removes repeated work for ZERO, FLOW and TAINT origins while keeping R4/R5 unchanged. It is the direction supported by current nonzero-owner evidence. No project factor-of-two claim follows from the interim sample alone.

stirling-small-demand-routing-design.text:
# Stirling run-5: remove repeated routing of unchanged packets

Status: source-backed design comparison. No runtime edits or new experiments. Latest completed iteration in the clean primary is run-5; run-6 stopped on its time limit. In the isolated diagnostic replay, run-4 is complete and run-5 is still active at this evidence cutoff (2026-10-29 22:53:21 UTC). The diagnostic replay has a different run-4 demand frontier; see `/tmp/stirling-small-demand-control-audit.md`. It is evidence about the diagnosed replay, not an exact reproduction of every clean-run state.

## 1. What is now established

The hot actor is `PipelineProcessor.runPipelineAgainstFiles(List, PipelineConfig)`. Its diagnostic counters at the cutoff are:

| Counter | Value |
|---|---:|
| Processed worklist packets | 1,118,253,712 |
| Changed / unchanged packet visits | 4,476,765 / 1,113,776,947 |
| Fresh initial facts: ZERO / FLOW / TAINT | 1 / 21 / 125 |
| Processed STATIC / other base packets | 330,731 / 1,117,922,981 |
| Maximum unfolded tree-node occurrences per observed packet | 7 |
| Packets with a protection mask | 0 |
| Repeat-set clears / nonempty clears | 4,476,764 / 4,376,639 |
| Nonempty clears while changed work remained | 4,376,638 |
| Maximum repeat-set size at a clear | 711 |
| Exact processed revisits across repeat-set epochs, in the bounded sample | 5,486,093 |

These are small, almost entirely nonstatic packets. The actor performs many visits to instructions which leave the packet unchanged. It does not need large packet trees to produce this work. The fresh-initial count does not bound the number of changed packet shapes or local bases.

The exact-repeat sample is deliberately biased: processing starts after one million visits; it samples nodes whose hash has six low zero bits; it uses an LRU of 256 exact keys; and it restricts the root/mask sizes. Its 5,486,093 witnesses are a lower bound in that sample domain. **They are not an estimate of the global duplicate fraction or the achievable speedup.** The larger unchanged count does not mean that all unchanged visits are duplicates: a fresh input must also cross neutral instructions once.

A witness processed in epochs 4722 and 4723 has the same node 464, whole premise and conclusion: premise `arg(0).[572,5796].*/T97`; conclusion `var(92).MapValue.Element.<rule-storage>.Element.[any]/T97`, DEMAND, empty field exclusion, no protection. T97 names the SSRF source mark. The saved diagnostic does not map IR node 464 to a precise Java source statement. Do not invent that mapping.

## 2. Exact source of the repetition opportunity

`DeltaWorklist.addUnchanged` records the whole `EdgeDelta` in `seen`. It adds a separate protection-mask component because ordinary `TaintTree.equals` omits that mask. `afterProcess()` clears `seen` whenever the unchanged queues are empty. It does so even if changed work remains. A changed packet can start another unchanged traversal through the same instructions, after the repeat ledger has forgotten the preceding traversal.

`RunMethodAnalyzer.process` still performs call detection and form handling for every such visit. `emitUnchanged` enumerates the successors and enqueues another unchanged packet. It avoids `MethodEdgeStore.add`, but it does not avoid CFG traversal, call-plan selection, rule checks, queue operations or repeat-key construction.

The hot Java method has nested loops over operations, files, extensions, map entries and lists. Branches merge inside these loops. A single packet can have many neutral paths through this CFG. This is a different issue from slow trie merging or large mark groups.

## 3. Option A: retain exact processing witnesses longer

### Minimal key and ownership

A cache owned by one method actor and one run can leave method/context, direction, field limit, rule view and frozen demand/native-record view implicit in its owner. It must be destroyed at the run boundary. Its explicit key is:

```kotlin
// Sketch. Use structural equality backed by canonical immutable nodes.
// A hash alone is never proof that the input is equal.
data class ExactVisit(
    val node: CommonInst,
    val premise: PremiseKey,        // complete canonical premise, including every ND member
    val facts: Facts,               // base, kind, layer, tail, E, FLOW mx, and full trie
    val protection: TaintNode?,     // required separately: Facts.equals omits this annotation
)
```

This key applies to ordinary method-worklist packets only. A resume event additionally has a `ResumeSite`, call stage, caller layer, identity classification, demotion state and completed action/conjunction state. Do not merge resume events into this cache by dropping those fields. Do not deduplicate only by initial mark, base, root identity, node, tree size or ordinary `Facts.equals`.

Two implementations are possible:

```kotlin
// Full-run exact history: strongest duplicate elimination, unbounded entry count.
if (completed.contains(fullKey)) return
processNormally(packet)              // complete observations and secure outgoing work
completed.add(fullKey)

// Bounded exact LRU: eviction only permits extra work; it never drops a new input.
if (recentCompleted.contains(fullKey)) return
processNormally(packet)
recentCompleted.put(fullKey)
```

These sketches require the idempotence proof below. They must not be installed at method entry admission, demand lookup or summary admission. Those operations must retain their existing contracts. A packet whose protection mask has grown is a different key and must run.

An in-flight/pending key can suppress a second equal enqueue only if the first queued item and its work reservation remain live until the first item is processed. Marking an arbitrary partly processed item as complete before its outputs are secured is invalid. On cancellation, discard this actor with its cache; never export the cache into another run.

### Safety and limitations

A full-run exact history needs no full trie **copy**, but its strong references retain packet roots at every visited point. Millions of changed packets multiplied by many instruction points can make it a new memory problem. The observed 147 initials and maximum seven-node packet do not bound that key count. It is not safe to recommend an unbounded per-point hash set solely from the bounded duplicate witnesses.

A bounded exact cache limits new retained state. It can miss duplicates after eviction. This changes performance, not the semantic result, provided each hit represents a semantically complete prior evaluation. Its actual hit ratio is unmeasured. The probe's LRU hit count used a different, biased node domain.

A smaller first change is to clear the existing repeat set only when the **whole** worklist is empty, rather than when its unchanged lane is empty. It retains witnesses through the observed changed/unchanged alternation, but does not cover later deliveries after actor quiescence. It still needs the same re-evaluation argument and a bound on the largest retained wave; it is not a proof of a fixed factor reduction.

The important proof is not merely that transfer is deterministic. Calls, predicates and joins own standing state. For a cached point input, prove all of the following:

- The first evaluation installs every needed call subscription and rule literal input. Later publications or other join members independently activate that standing state. They do not need a repeat of the original packet.
- Rule source/sink identities, seed occurrences and stop observations are unchanged. Duplicate callback counts and profiling counters are not semantic identities. If a user callback requires each visit, use the existing route instead.
- The rule/form, demand and native-record views stay fixed for this run. Any mutable dependency which can change the result either has its own standing replay mechanism or must invalidate/bypass the cache.
- The cache distinguishes all premise/context and protection states. In later forward runs ND premises remain complete; in backward runs ZERO keeps its existing exception and phase policy.
- Alias application, cleaning, source assignment, layer changes, cuts and summary publication still occur once for every distinct complete input. A cache must not use a current FLOW cover as proof that a previously protected TAINT input was processed.

`ConjunctionStore` does retain literal inputs and recomputes complete bindings when a different member or annotation changes. `SubscriptionManager` retains qualified current inputs and delivers later publications. Those source structures support the argument, but a formal end-to-end idempotence proof is still required before a general cache can skip stateful points.

For a conservative first implementation, cache only inputs at a proved observationally neutral point. Then a cache hit skips only identity routing; no stateful evaluator is skipped. This reduces the proof surface, but may remove fewer visits.

## 4. Option B: jump across a certified neutral CFG region

This avoids paying for every neutral instruction even for a genuinely fresh packet. It need not retain the full packet at every skipped point.

### Neutrality certificate

Start with restricted runs (run-2 and later). Leave run-1 batching, static service, requests and point-resume behavior unchanged. For a selected packet base `b`, an instruction is neutral only when its actual current transfer is:

```text
(premise, facts) -> the same (premise, facts) at every CFG successor
```

and it has no source/sink, rule-join, boundary, summary, alias, resume or stop observation for that packet. Certify this against the actual interpreter, not from a source-level guess that a variable is unused.

Concrete safe gates to develop are:

```kotlin
fun neutral(node: CommonInst, b: AccessPathBase): Boolean {
    if (context.isEnd(node) || context.isExceptionalExit(node)) return false
    val call = context.callAt(node)
    if (call != null) {
        // REACH/ZERO is excluded from this certificate.
        // Reuse the exact existing CallPlan.touched gate.
        return b != ZERO && b !in callPlan(node).touched
    }
    val s = statementSummary(node)
    return b != ZERO && b !in s.touched &&
        s.conjunctions.isEmpty() && s.sources.isEmpty()
    // Also require no external per-node observation hook, or fall back.
}
```

This is a conservative starting certificate, not production code. The statement checks are intentional: `FormApplier.statement` evaluates conjunctions and source predicates even when the input base is absent from `s.touched`. In contrast, `RunMethodCallServices.process` already emits an untouched non-REACH call input unchanged when its base is absent from the complete call plan's `touched` set. In later runs, `EngineAlgebra.reached` has no run-1 static-point operation effect. Exceptional exits and normal exits remain observable barriers.

A more precise certificate can use base-qualified predicate metadata later. Do not silently omit rule predicates merely because a micro-edge does not change this base. Do not add local-liveness pruning, field abstraction changes or a different alias policy under the name of neutral routing.

### Branches, loops and storage

For one actor and one base, use the analyzer's **oriented CFG**. Reverse runs use the reversed successors. Contract neutral strongly connected components, or use an equivalent visited traversal. Preserve all ordinary and exceptional successors.

```kotlin
fun route(start: CommonInst, packet: EdgeDelta) {
    val todo = dequeOf(start)
    val visited = BitSet(numberOfCfgNodes) // metadata only, local to this routing invocation
    while (todo.isNotEmpty()) {
        cancellation.checkpoint()
        val n = todo.removeFirst()
        if (visited[n.id]) continue
        visited[n.id] = true
        if (!neutral(n, packet.facts.base)) {
            enqueueOrdinary(packet.copy(node = n))
        } else {
            context.forEachSuccessor(n) { todo.add(it) }
        }
    }
}
```

The sketch is sound reachability routing but still visits every neutral node once per call. It is a correctness baseline, not the desired speed improvement. The optimized form caches the **first observable frontier** of a neutral region/SCC, as CFG metadata only, and enqueues the unchanged packet at that frontier directly. It does not retain a facts trie at each interior node.

- A neutral branch emits the same packet at each distinct first observable successor. It must not arbitrarily choose a branch.
- A neutral cycle with exits routes to each reachable observable frontier. A closed neutral cycle has no transfer output or observation and contributes no frontier.
- A cycle which includes a rule, call effect or write stops at that barrier. The ordinary evaluator handles it. Do not jump through it on an identity assumption.
- A barrier does not combine different premises, contexts, packet headers or masks. It uses the existing admission/unchanged queue behavior at the correct target point.
- A lazy cache for a base/region stores only CFG/frontier metadata. Avoid a dense all-bases × all-nodes × all-frontiers table. Bound or evict this metadata cache; eviction can recompute routes safely.
- Frontier traversal and cache construction must yield/check cancellation, retain the actor's current work reservation and not cross a commit/freeze boundary as uncounted work.

A neutral region may have many frontiers. Its route table may be larger than its node set. Measure that geometry; contraction does not automatically make an all-pairs closure cheap. Start with single-exit neutral chains/SCCs or a lazy frontier representation if necessary.

The method has many calls. Requiring every call to be a barrier could leave short regions. Reusing the existing untouched-call gate is therefore useful, but the actual neutral-region lengths and frontier widths are not yet measured. There is no justified factor-of-two claim yet.

### Example: what work disappears

```java
// Existing packet J at local x: p.*/T -> x.[any]/T, DEMAND.
// The loop/branch tests and assignments below have neutral certificates for x.
while (operationsRemain()) {          // A: certified untouched call for x
    int n = operationIndex;          // B: neutral for x
    if (hasMoreFiles) {              // C: neutral branch for x
        int f = fileIndex;           // D: neutral for x
    } else {
        int e = errorCount;          // E: neutral for x
    }
    consume(x);                      // F: observable barrier, processed as usual
}
// Neither A--E's neutrality nor the loop's branch condition means F can be skipped.
```

This is a schematic CFG example, not a claim that these are the saved IR nodes 464/564. Suppose `N` distinct complete packets enter at A, the neutral region has `L` visited instruction points per traversal, and it has `K` distinct first observable frontiers. Original routing costs at least `N*L` point visits before barriers, plus exact repeated traversals after epoch clears. A cached route removes the neutral point visits and forwards at most `N*K` unchanged packets to those frontiers, plus route metadata work. If `L=100`, `K=2`, `N=1,000`, that is 100,000 neutral visits versus 2,000 frontier enqueues after one route computation. These are illustrative counts; the actual Pipeline values of L, K and N remain unknown.

Exact completed-visit caching and neutral routing address different terms. A safe exact cache removes repeated equal inputs. A route removes neutral intermediate visits for new inputs too. A cache only at observable frontier points may combine the benefits with fewer retained packet keys than per-instruction durable history, but it still needs the stateful-observation proof from option A.

## 5. Proof and validation obligations before selection

Follow `spec/proof-guide.md`: constructive Lean model first, optimized/reference equivalence, then focused tests. This note has not completed those proofs and is not implementation authorization.

1. **Scope:** no semantic change to AP grammar, exclusions, field reads/writes, demands, initial emission, protected-edge propagation, source/sink joins, aliases or run boundaries. Profiling visit counts may decrease. Declare any additional observation contract explicitly.
2. **Exact-key adequacy:** equality of the key entails equality of every input and annotation used by transfer. Prove the protection-mask upgrade case separately.
3. **Standing-state idempotence:** if a stateful point can be cached, prove a later dependency wakes it without needing a duplicate input evaluation. Construct witnesses for both subscription-before-publication and publication-before-subscription races, nonlinear joins and protection upgrades.
4. **Neutrality:** for every permitted certificate, construct the exact identity-transfer witness and the empty-observation witness. An untouched statement with a source or conjunction is a required negative test.
5. **Route equivalence:** by induction on CFG paths and finite SCC reachability, every reference path reaches the same first observable barrier with the same complete packet; every optimized barrier enqueue has a reference path. Cover branches, exceptional edges, loops and backward traversal.
6. **Completion:** route work is counted, cancellation-aware and frozen only after all outputs are secured. A bounded cache's eviction only adds work; it cannot cause a false cache hit or lose a pending packet.
7. **Operational test:** retain a loop/branch regression with one neutral path, one effectful path, late callee publication and a mask-only upgrade. Compare normal/demand summaries, report identities/occurrences, seeds and stop observations; do not compare raw callback counts as semantic results.
8. **Measurement:** on the isolated replay, record actor-local exact cache admissions/hits/evictions, visited neutral nodes, region/frontier widths, distinct complete packet keys and retained bytes. Compare run-5 and run-6. Do not infer run-6 protection-mask cost from this protection-free run-5 actor alone.

## Recommendation

The least risky immediate design experiment is a longer-lived, bounded **exact** unchanged-visit witness cache, first restricted to certified neutral inputs, plus a proof of the current repeat-reset lifetime. It directly targets observed cross-epoch revisits without unbounded per-point retention. Certified neutral-region routing is the stronger structural candidate for fresh packet routing. Prefer it over a persistent full fact tree at every CFG instruction if the measured neutral frontiers are narrow. Neither change is yet measured; do not promise a whole-engine factor reduction.

# Review of the Stirling small-demand report

Reviewed 2026-10-29, read-only. Draft: `docs/reports/bidirectional-stirling-small-demand-workload-20261029.md`. Runtime reference `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`.

Result: no blocking correctness issue in the proposed scope. The draft separates the clean campaign from the diagnostic replay, states the different run-4 frontier, avoids a speedup comparison, preserves native R4/R5, and makes join/protection/publication proofs prerequisites for a work-removal design. Running counters are provisional as requested.

Suggested concise changes:

1. In section 3, replace “does not come from large packets” with “does not come from large spatial fact trees in this observed owner.” The probe logs maximum trie-node occurrences, not full mark-membership width or retained bytes. A seven-node tree can still carry several marks at a leaf.
2. Replace “or static fact routing” with “or a large count of direct STATIC-fact visits.” The current conclusion-base counter does not establish that every expensive nonstatic fact has a nonstatic origin. The overwhelming nonzero-premise claim *is* independently supported by the logged `processedPremise_ZERO_FLOW_TAINT` counters.
3. Add one sentence before/after the queue model: “The two pending packets start at distinct admitted points and reach the common join through unchanged successors. If two changed transfers directly submit equal F to the same point, MethodEdgeStore already deduplicates them.” This makes the finite witness's scope explicit and avoids implying that the durable changed gate is broken.
4. In section 1, make the attribution explicitly diagnostic: “The dominant owner observed in diagnostic run-5 performs repeated work with nonzero initials.” This keeps the first conclusion consistent with the later warning that the clean and diagnostic run-4 frontiers differ. The source mechanism applies to the same runtime, but identical project event traces have not been established.
5. In section 6, name the 3,719 roots as the configured roots (public/protected UNKNOWN roots plus generated Spring roots), rather than describing all of them as public/protected roots. The direct root ZERO attempts are not counted by restricted C2 intersections.

Verified controls:

* The isolated `SmallDemandNativeNeutralWorkTest` XML records one passing test, no failure/error, at 22:42:07 UTC. Its actual observations are: no-native N=1/9 has noise steps 3/11 and marked-neutral steps 0/0; native N=1/9 has noise steps 5/21, one record crossing in each, and marked-neutral steps 1/9. The exact “eight additional marked visits” statement is supported. This is a mechanism fixture, not a Stirling speedup measurement.
* Run-5 ordinary growth is `189337 - 33836 = 155501`.
* Run-6 ordinary accepted input deltas are `581374 - 17724 = 563650`; ordinary growth is `563650 - 8910 = 554740`, about 98.42%; accepted deltas/new group is about 63.26. Do not equate this with a duplicate-input percentage.
* The bounded witness keeps full premise/fact equality and an explicit protection mask. It proves sampled complete-key repeats across reset epochs, not their global frequency or blanket redundancy of all equal-looking facts.

Keep the current proof gates. In particular, a persistent or region-level repeat gate must preserve fresh protection upgrades, future mixed joins, standing subscriptions, rule observations, and fair delivery. The report does not claim these proofs are already complete.

No report, production code, analyzer configuration, or live process was changed by this review.

# Stirling PipelineProcessor trace

Clean runtime: `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`. The separate diagnostic checkout adds passive counters only. The clean campaign reached run-6, completed run-5, and accepted the run-5 forward report. The diagnostic run-5 also completed; its final actor counters are quoted below. Run-6 diagnostic work was still active when this note was prepared.

## Actual owner and workload

The hot actor is:

```text
stirling.software.SPDF.controller.api.pipeline.PipelineProcessor
  #runPipelineAgainstFiles(java.util.List, PipelineConfig) [{}]
run-5, FORWARD, field limit4, FULL marks
```

Its final diagnostic run-5 counters are:

```text
process entries:       1,581,415,551
unchanged entries:     1,575,082,922
changed entries:           6,332,629
sampled exact accepted/processed revisits across repeat epochs: 7,751,326
```

The diagnostic run-5 engine is 650.857s. Do not use this instrumented time as a replacement for the clean 612.328s measurement.

At the second progress sample,22:46:01.640:

```text
steps45,402,712; changed184,161; unchanged45,218,551
fresh initials: ZERO1, FLOW21, TAINT125
processed static28,707; other45,374,005
maximum ordinary trie size7; protection packets0
nonempty repeat-set clears179,139
nonempty clears with changed work pending179,138
sampled exact processed revisits216,313
```

This is about 245.54 unchanged process entries per changed entry at that sample. The packet trees are small. The expensive part is repeated instruction processing of small relations. This is not an explanation based on large individual trees, cleaners, or protection masks for run-5.

## The actual source

File:

```text
/drive-testcomp/opentaint-go-rules/e2e-root/model-Stirling-PDF/sources/
  app/core/src/main/java/stirling/software/SPDF/controller/api/pipeline/PipelineProcessor.java
```

The source has nested container loops. The principal multi-input part is source lines197–211:

```java
MultiValueMap<String, Object> body = new LinkedMultiValueMap<>();
for (Resource file : matchingFiles) {       // Source199.
    body.add("fileInput", file);             // Source200.
}
// Measured fact at IR464:
// I944 -> body.MapValue.Iterable.Element.Collection.<rule-storage>.Iterable.Element.[any]/T
// DEMAND; T is the SSRF UNTRUSTED full mark; protection is empty.
for (Entry<String, Object> entry : parameters.entrySet()) { // Source202.
    if (entry.getValue() instanceof List<?> entryList) {
        for (Object item : entryList) {
            body.add(entry.getKey(), item);
        }
    } else {
        body.add(entry.getKey(), entry.getValue());
    }
}
ResponseEntity<byte[]> response = sendWebRequest(url, body);
```

The outer method also has:

```java
for (PipelineOperation pipelineOperation : config.getOperations()) { // Source98.
    // Non-multi branch:
    // outputFiles loop × inputFileTypes loop × parameters loop × entryList loop.
    // Multi branch: matchingFiles loop, then parameters and entryList loops.
    ...
    outputFiles = newOutputFiles;            // Source252.
}                                           // Source253: outer backedge.
```

The analyzer explores the CFG branches. These source collection lengths are not execution bounds for the analysis.

## Verified instruction and variable mapping

The analyzed class bytes are present in both c0 and c5. Their SHA-256 is identical:

```text
e3108900ac3cf7655de5658772c903eee071a22985a8b86fc4d4812635abfa77
```

A small standalone IR metadata reader used the actual class bytes. It ran with one active processor and a 1GiB heap. It did not run the analyzer, attach to the live JVM, or modify its compiled artifacts.

| Diagnostic value | Actual IR/source meaning |
|---|---|
| node75 | Source120: outputFiles iterator `hasNext` condition; successors76 and419. |
| node430 | Source180: branch on `inputFileTypes.contains("ALL")`; successors435 and431. |
| node464 | Source202: `%95 = %87.entrySet()` where `%87` is parameters; successor465. |
| var92 | Multi-input `body`; allocation443, constructor444, file-input add462, copy to var115 at483. |
| var58 | `matchingFiles`; branch definitions433/439, reads441/445, copy456. |
| var113 | A loop-carried `newOutputFiles` local; definition481, later loop copies and use591. |

The read at464 reads parameters, not body. `JIRCallPlanBuilder.touched()` includes S, its receiver, arguments and result. For this call those direct nonstatic bases are parameters and var95, not var92. `RunMethodCallServices.process` therefore takes the existing `emitUnchanged` path for the measured var92 fact.

Nodes75 and430 are branch instructions. `JIRStatementForms.build` gives these non-assignment/non-return/non-throw instructions an empty statement form. Their measured unrelated local facts pass unchanged through the existing path.

The numeric initial accessor IDs572 and5796 were not mapped to names. They belong to the live AP manager's accessor table; the current probe prints its initial path as IDs. The standalone IR reader cannot recover that table's allocation order. Do not infer names from the numbers or use a different manager's IDs as substitutes.

## Transformations and mapping proof boundary

The reader uses keep-local-variable-names, the current lambda transformer, string-concat transformer and method-boundary feature. A minimal Spring context contains the ApiDocService component and its field dependency in PipelineProcessor.

The first form has 697 instructions with the lambda, concat and boundary transforms. Three ApiDocService reads at25/31/40 each become a goto plus an appended five-instruction Spring block. With the Spring feature before the boundary feature, the reproduced method has 712 instructions; entry/normal/exceptional boundaries are709/710/711.

```text
25 ->694: null / non-det bool / branch / registry read / back to26
31 ->699: null / non-det bool / branch / registry read / back to32
40 ->704: null / non-det bool / branch / registry read / back to41
```

`JSingleInstructionTransformer.generateReplacementBlock` retains the original location and replaces it with a goto. `BlockGenerationContext.addInstruction` uses the current list size for each appended instruction. The lambda transformer uses the same append-and-goto pattern. Thus these later feature blocks do not renumber the original75/430/464 positions or their original local IDs.

This is a method-body metadata reconstruction, not a second full Spring prescan. It does not reconstruct the live accessor table, all resolved callees, rule bindings, aliases, or actual dynamic producer order. The selected original instruction mappings do not require those append-only Spring blocks to have a particular registry target.

## Local control routes and repeated work

The matching-file loop is:

```text
458: iterator.hasNext
459: branch ->460 or464
460: iterator.next
461: cast Resource
462: body.add("fileInput", file)
463: goto458
```

The parameter-loop entry is:

```text
464: parameters.entrySet
465: entrySet.iterator
466..482: loop-carried local copies
483: var115 = var92      // Copy the body; this operation reads var92.
484: copy iterator
485: goto486
486: iterator.hasNext
487: branch ->488 or586
```

For the measured body fact at464,464..482 do not read or assign var92. They are unchanged hops until483. At483 the existing local move keeps the source and transfers to its new local. Its outputs use the ordinary changed-result path and successor store.

The method's outer backedge is642->20. This allows facts from inner processing to reach other branches and loop entries again until a relevant overwrite or transfer stops them. A local fact that is irrelevant at one branch can still incur instruction, form, CFG and repeat-gate work there.

The two admission paths are different:

```text
changed result:
  MethodEdgeStore.add(successor, full premise, facts)
  -> only a fresh returned delta becomes changed work

unchanged result:
  worklist.addUnchanged(successor, full premise, facts)
  -> no MethodEdgeStore admission at that successor
```

`DeltaWorklist.afterProcess` clears the unchanged repeat set when all unchanged lanes are empty, even if changed work remains. A later changed wave can therefore traverse an already-processed unchanged relation at the same node again. The diagnostic detects this with full node, premise, Facts and protection equality, not a hash-only test.

The first measured exact witness is:

```text
oldEpoch4722 -> newEpoch4723
node464
initial I944: arg0 / path[572,5796] / STAR / concrete full mark97
conclusion: var92 / DEMAND / ANY / Empty E
path: Map#MapValue.Iterable#Element.Collection#<rule-storage>.Iterable#Element
mark97: java/security/ssrf.yaml:ssrf#source#1;0;$UNTRUSTED;2
protection: none
```

This proves an identical body relation is processed at that same instruction in different unchanged epochs. The repeat sample is restricted to node-hash low six bits zero, actor steps>=1M, root/mask size<=1,024, and a256-entry LRU. Its count is a lower bound, not an extrapolated project repetition rate.

The exact predecessor changed point for each witness was not recorded. It is not valid to assert that all 6.3M changed entries are duplicate facts. They can be fresh at different point-store locations or carry new memberships. The measured redundancy is that those waves cause already-processed unchanged relations elsewhere to execute again. The source copy/loop structure explains where these long unchanged routes exist; the exact producer pair for the first464 witness remains unobserved.

## Meaning for the small-demand question

The 13,901 incoming selected demands gate run-5 initial admission. They do not provide an intra-method visited-membership set at every instruction. One actor with 146 fresh nonzero initials and one ZERO initial can then execute 1.58 billion instruction entries, most of which are unchanged, and still export only 1,304 selected demand memberships.

The actual new finding is repeated local processing caused by the short repeat-set lifetime and the absence of unchanged membership admission at each point. It is not that 13,901 demand intersections themselves take 612s. The next design must avoid re-executing equal unchanged relations and/or skip proved irrelevant routes. It must retain needed source/rule/call/boundary observations.
