# Stirling run-6: mixed model-field chains

Date: 2026-10-29. Runtime reference: `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`.
The isolated diagnostic replay is closed: latest reached run-6, latest complete run-5; run-6 TIMEOUT. This note uses source inspection and the closed scalar probe log. No runtime change, build, analyzer, or heavy reader was launched.

The parent's final run-6 census has 7,257 actors and about 217 million steps: 99.536% use ZERO premises and 99.883% have nonstatic conclusions. Of 736,382 protected packets, 724,385 occur in the two settings-update methods. The representative owner below is a source/model trace target within that census; its own 362,213 steps are not the whole run.

## Finding

The apparent field alphabet has a direct source in library pass-through models. Ordinary backward reversal can prepend each of these named model fields. This is not evidence that the analyzer found actual Pair or StrTokenizer objects in the controller. The backward interpreter deliberately drops type filters. Alias analysis can further unite alternative model paths, but the particular captured chain has not been traced to a specific alias application.

Do not treat every mixed-owner chain as impossible. `ImmutablePair.left`, `MutablePair.right`, and `StrTokenizer.<rule-storage>` all have modeled value type `java.lang.Object`. Their concatenation can pass a declared-type check between those slots. The more discriminating example is a StrTokenizer field immediately below the known `ConcurrentHashMap`-typed `pendingChanges` field.

## Closed diagnostic evidence

`AdminSettingsController#updateSettingsSection(String,Map)` at run-6 timeout:

```text
steps=362213 changed=116541 unchanged=245672
freshZero=1 freshFlow=0 freshTaint=0
processedPremise_ZERO_FLOW_TAINT=[362213,0,0]
processedKind_REACH_FLOW_TAINT=[213,0,362000]
processedBase_STATIC_OTHER=[537,361676]
recordCrossings=12318 protectedPackets=361804
maxTreeNodeOccurrences=7 maxMaskNodeOccurrences=7
pending changed packets=26799
```

Representative final local path (T93 is the XSS rule's full mark):

```text
ZERO -> var31.MutablePair.left.MutablePair.left.StrTokenizer.<rule-storage>
              .ImmutablePair.right.HeaderElementIterator.<rule-storage>.[any]/T93
DEMAND; the same path is protected.
```

Largest spatial path seen in this owner:

```text
ZERO -> S.AdminSettingsController.pendingChanges
          .StrTokenizer.<rule-storage>.StrTokenizer.<rule-storage>
          .StrTokenizer.<rule-storage>.StrTokenizer.<rule-storage>.[any]/T93
DEMAND; the same path is protected.
```

The field budget is five counted fields: `pendingChanges` plus four storage fields; the static class accessor is not counted. Every `<rule-storage>` is an ordinary counted `FieldAccessor` in this core (`bidi/ap/AccessorTable.kt:58`). These are many small paths, not a single deep unbounded packet. The seven-node maximum does not measure all distinct path candidates across operations.

## 1. Exact model generators

`model/java/config/org.apache.commons-commons-lang3-3.14.0.yaml`:

| Source lines | Model | Read fields which the reverse can prepend |
|---|---|---|
| 382–401 | `Pair#getLeft`, `Pair#getValue` | `ImmutablePair.left` or `MutablePair.left`; `ImmutablePair.right` or `MutablePair.right` |
| 1017–1026 | `Pair#getKey` | `ImmutablePair.left`, `MutablePair.left` |
| 1059–1068 | `Pair#getRight` | `ImmutablePair.right`, `MutablePair.right` |
| 833–840 | `StrTokenizer#next` | both raw `this -> result` and `this.StrTokenizer.<rule-storage>/Object -> result` |
| 1913–1920 | `StrTokenizer#getTokenList` | the same raw/storage pair |

Other members of the observed alphabet:

* `model/java/config/stdlib/java-util.yaml:2479–2486`: `Map.Entry#getKey` reads the synthetic `Map.Entry.Key/Object` field.
* `java-util.yaml:5636–5643`: `Iterator#next` reads `Iterator.Element/Object`.
* `model/java/config/org.apache.httpcomponents-httpcore-4.4.16.yaml:311–322`: the `HeaderElementIterator#next.*` pattern reads its synthetic `<rule-storage>/Object` and also copies raw receiver taint to the result.

These synthetic fields represent model storage. Some are not Java-declared fields. Their names alone cannot establish actual heap layout.

## 2. Why generic interface calls can see subtype models

`MethodClassTaintRulesStorage.kt:157–173` pushes a subtype model to matching supertype methods with a generated `typeIs(Subtype,this)` condition. `findRules` also searches supertypes and known subclasses (`176–191`). Thus an `Iterator.next` call can obtain a StrTokenizer implementation model; a `Map.Entry.getKey/getValue` call can obtain Pair models.

This is guarded, not unconditional, in ordinary taint forms. `JIRCallPlanBuilder.passRules:318–348` rewrites each condition for the concrete call site, skips a false condition, and builds its copy micro-edges. A generic declared receiver such as Iterator or Map.Entry may admit more than one implementation type. `JIRBasicAtomEvaluator.typeMatchesPattern:322–354` uses declared receiver type compatibility; it does not prove the runtime iterator allocation is StrTokenizer. It includes an explicit Object-type fallback rejection, so do not describe this as universally accepting every Object model.

`JIRRuleForms.pass:553–570` lowers `CopyAllMarks` to a STAR-to-STAR micro-edge. For a read model this has the precise operator shape below:

```text
Forward model:  this.storage.*/FLOW -> ret.*/FLOW
Backward model: ret.*/FLOW          -> this.storage.*/FLOW

Provided backward ret.sigma.[any]/T93, DEMAND:
result:           this.storage.sigma.[any]/T93, DEMAND
```

The existing protection annotation follows the marked transfer. The field cut bounds the resulting word; it does not validate adjacent declaring types.

This identifies a real operator which adds the observed field names. It does **not** yet prove the full local-base routing which repeats the operator four times in this exact owner. A loop by itself does not prove the same receiver/result relation can be reapplied. That link may involve aliases, raw model arms, previously retained native paths, or other model calls. The next useful trace is the changed operation which first constructs each longer path, not another wall-clock profile.

## 3. Backward type filtering is deliberately absent

`StatementSummary.reversed:59–68` reverses the micro-edges and constructs the backward form with an empty operand-filter map and no result-filter map:

```kotlin
val back = StatementSummary(touched + targets, rev, emptyList(), emptyMap(),
                            sources = sources.map { it.reversed() })
```

This follows `spec/interpreter.md` I5: backward runs apply no type filter. It is not a regression introduced by the passive probe. `JIRCallPlanBuilder` normally attaches receiver/argument/result filters at bindings (`178–209`) and declared base filters to pass forms (`345–347`); ordinary reversal drops them.

Enabling existing forward filters backwards would also be insufficient as a whole-chain validator. `JIRFactTypeChecker.AccessorFilter` accepts a compatible FieldAccessor without a `FilterNext` transition to its declared value type (`100–106`). `bidi/ap/Filter.kt:74` keeps that entire child subtree for Accept. Static class prefixes also accept; static alias destinations have no result filters (`JIRCallPlanBuilder.aliases:350–367`).

A new typed-word validity check would therefore need explicit transitions through each field, not simply a reversed filter map.

## 4. Alias amplification: source-confirmed capability, unproved captured producer

`JIRLocalAliasAnalysis.CallModelProvider:74–89` requests original pass-through rules, flattens all their CopyAllMarks actions, and emits ExternalAssigns. It does not retain/evaluate their rule conditions. These are ordinary original metadata rules, not run-1 group rewrites.

`DSUAliasAnalysis.evalExternalCallModel:183–190` unites each assignment's source and target alias sets. With the two StrTokenizer arms, the available relation is:

```text
this ~ result
this.storage ~ result
therefore this ~ this.storage
```

Likewise, alternative Pair fields copied to one result can become one alias component. `JIRIntraProcAliasAnalysis.Convert:103–131` converts these heap aliases back into field paths with a finite heap-chain limit of five. New-core call alias forms copy their full paths (`JIRCallPlanBuilder.aliases:350–367`) and do not type-filter the static outputs. This is a credible route for self-storage prefixes and cross-product paths.

Do not claim it generated the captured `pendingChanges` path until a source-bound form/operation trace confirms the relevant persisted alias paths. The original model-to-reference-alias interpretation itself needs an explicit contract: copying marks between positions does not by itself establish physical Java reference equality.

## 5. Concrete declared-type contradiction to investigate

The real controller source has:

```java
private static final ConcurrentHashMap<String,Object> pendingChanges =
    new ConcurrentHashMap<>();                                  // lines 63–64

for (Map.Entry<String,Object> entry : sectionData.entrySet()) { // lines 313–327
    String propertyKey = entry.getKey();
    Object value = entry.getValue();
    GeneralUtils.saveKeyToSettings(sectionName + "." + propertyKey, value);
    pendingChanges.put(fullKey, value);
}
```

For actual Java fields, the captured adjacency is:

```text
...pendingChanges : ConcurrentHashMap
     .StrTokenizer.<rule-storage> : Object
```

If `<rule-storage>` is a receiver-owned modeled slot, its receiver must be a possible StrTokenizer. ConcurrentHashMap and StrTokenizer are unrelated concrete classes, so no Java object can be a subtype of both. This does not require `pendingChanges` to be final or an allocation-sensitive alias proof. Its declared concrete field type is sufficient.

The current checker's public `typeMayHaveSubtypeOf(typeName,requiredTypeName)` implements this test: for two resolved classes it requires one class to be a subclass of the other (`JIRFactTypeChecker:276–315`). With these known unrelated classes it would reject the adjacency. Missing class metadata conservatively returns true. This is a source-level derivation, not a newly executed hierarchy test.

In contrast, this local word has no such contradiction from its declarations alone:

```text
ImmutablePair.left/Object -> MutablePair.right/Object -> StrTokenizer.storage/Object
```

Every Object slot could hold the next receiver type. Do not drop it merely because the class names look unrelated.

## 6. Next trace and required contract

Before an optimization, capture/derive the first producer operation for:

1. `pendingChanges.storage`;
2. `pendingChanges.storage.storage`;
3. a Pair/Tokenizer mixed local prefix.

Keep source MethodKey, node, call target, stage kind, exact input/output paths, original premise, layer and protection. Distinguish reversed PASS_RULES, reversed ALIASES, native-record application and ordinary micro-edges. This will identify the missing base-routing link without a broad new cache or a new run-wide leaf enumeration.

A behavior decision is needed before early typed pruning:

> Is each model FieldAccessor, including `<rule-storage>`, a receiver-owned abstract slot which must satisfy the declared-owner/value-type chain? Or can synthetic storage be a transparent taint annotation which intentionally crosses those type boundaries?

For the first interpretation, specify and prove typed validity for ordinary models, aliases, static prefixes, generic Object slots and unknown metadata. Then early rejection of a proved incompatible adjacency removes an entire family of impossible path words. It must preserve all required demand edges for valid modeled paths. For the second interpretation, Java heap-type rejection is not automatically valid; model storage/alias semantics must change first.

This is a possible major semantic change. Do not silently enable backward filters, forbid all mixed-owner words, change selected-cleaner behavior, or remove protection. The work-removal goal is to prevent impossible candidate families, not to make each rejected path faster. No multiplicative project saving has yet been measured for this family.

Source SHA-256 bindings are in `/tmp/stirling-run6-mixed-field-chain-sources.json` (12 source/model/project files). Runtime source was read from the main checkout; the closed probe remains diagnostic evidence only.

Run-6: 217,127,496 processed; 186,388,894 unchanged (**85.843063%**); 216,119,741 ZERO-premise (**99.535869%**); 216,872,413 nonstatic (**99.882519%**). All tabled owner counts match, including **updateSettingsSection unchanged=245,672**. Settings protection sums to **724,385**, or **98.370818%** of 736,382 protected packets. Primary versus diagnostic frontiers, final engine times and latest labels agree with the embedded closed logs. ## Scope and evidence checks

- The report explicitly rejects a global duplicate percentage or speedup inference from the biased bounded witness sample.

- Current native callback counts and CPU sample denominators are kept separate. Inclusive profile shares are identified as overlapping.

- The metadata reconstruction is described as selected-transformer class reconstruction, not a replay of the full live prescan. Accessor IDs are not assigned invented names.
- There is **no authorization for field/type pruning**, ZERO removal or demand-gating all native reuse. The mixed synthetic paths remain trace targets requiring a contract and proof.
- Proposed routing and retained-boundary designs are separate future work. They do not claim an implemented optimization or measured two-times speedup.
- Production runtime diff fields are empty, local report links resolve, the isolated test XML has one test with four controls and zero failures/errors, and latest-run labels are explicit.

One nonblocking data limitation: the 7,257 rows contain **7,254 distinct rendered method strings**, with three colliding pairs (`User#getAuthorities`, and `JwtSaml2AuthenticationRequestRepository#loadAuthenticationRequest` / `removeAuthenticationRequest`). Printed method strings are not unique actor identifiers. No rows were removed when recomputing totals. This does not invalidate the report's actor-row totals; future per-actor joins must retain row identity or full descriptors rather than use this string as a unique key.

"""Finite executable model of the later-run changed/unchanged lane ordering.
Not an analyzer run or a claim about the actual hot method.
"""
from collections import Counter
import json

def witness(source_count, chain_length, cycle=False):
    # Each changed source is admitted at its own node before this experiment.
    changed=[('source',i) for i in range(source_count)]
    unchanged=[]
    seen=set()
    processed=Counter()
    repeat_rejects=0
    clears=0
    observations=set()
    def offer(node):
        nonlocal repeat_rejects
        key=('same_complete_premise','same_fact_and_protection',node)
        if key in seen:repeat_rejects+=1;return
        seen.add(key);unchanged.append(node)
    while changed or unchanged:
        if unchanged:
            node=unchanged.pop();processed[f'chain-{node}']+=1
            if node+1<chain_length:offer(node+1)
            elif cycle:offer(0)
            else:observations.add('same_sink_identity')
        else:
            node=changed.pop();processed['changed_sources']+=1;offer(0)
        # Exact source condition: DeltaWorklist.afterProcess checks only
        # unchanged lanes, not whether changed work remains.
        if not unchanged:
            seen.clear();clears+=1
    return {'sources':source_count,'chainLength':chain_length,'closedCycle':cycle,
      'changedProcesses':processed['changed_sources'],'unchangedProcesses':sum(v for k,v in processed.items() if k.startswith('chain-')),
      'eachCommonNodeVisits':[processed[f'chain-{i}'] for i in range(chain_length)],
      'repeatRejects':repeat_rejects,'repeatSetClears':clears,'uniqueSinkObservations':len(observations),'terminalQueueEmpty':True}

out={'modelScope':'Same one immutable complete premise/fact/protection packet from distinct admitted changed nodes; no ZERO control, filters, calls, or new transfer rules.',
 'finiteFanIn':witness(2,3),'hundredSources':witness(100,100),'oneSourceClosedNeutralCycle':witness(1,3,True),'twoSourcesClosedNeutralCycle':witness(2,3,True)}
assert out['finiteFanIn']['unchangedProcesses']==6
assert out['hundredSources']['unchangedProcesses']==10000
assert out['oneSourceClosedNeutralCycle']['unchangedProcesses']==3
assert out['oneSourceClosedNeutralCycle']['repeatRejects']==1
assert out['twoSourcesClosedNeutralCycle']['unchangedProcesses']==6
print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
